title: Voice never connects: the RTC socket goes to wss://127.0.0.1:3004 and nothing listens there
steps: 1. Run scripts/dev/worktree-setup.sh 3145 <db>. 2. Log in as tester and open Test Guild. 3. Create a voice channel 'General' (type 2). 4. Click it.
observed: The voice panel shows 'Connecting' (yellow), then flips to 'Disconnected' (red), and the client keeps retrying. The console shows: WebSocket connection to 'wss://127.0.0.1:3004/?v=9' failed. VOICE_SERVER_UPDATE carries endpoint "127.0.0.1:3004". server.log shows '[WebRTC] Failed to import undefined: No library configured in .env' and '[WebRTC] WEBRTC disabled'. Nothing listens on 3004 or on WRTC_WS_PORT (4145). The client then sends science events voice_connection_socket_failure and voice_disconnect.
expected: The panel should reach 'Voice Connected' with a working RTC connection, as in Discord.
evidence: Gateway frames: VOICE_SERVER_UPDATE {"token":"42f4102890e79f17","guild_id":"1555568719667658893","endpoint":"127.0.0.1:3004"}. The client hardcodes the protocol with `let to=/^https/.test("https:")?"wss:":"ws:"` (web.ea428454da038edc.js), so it always uses wss://, even on an http dev instance.
suspected_cause: There are three separate problems. First, worktree-setup.sh never sets WRTC_LIBRARY, and @spacebarchat/pion-webrtc is not installed in node_modules, so src/webrtc/util/MediaServer.ts disables WebRTC, yet src/gateway/opcodes/VoiceStateUpdate.ts still sends VOICE_SERVER_UPDATE. Second, the default region endpoint in src/util/config/types/RegionConfiguration.ts is hardcoded to 127.0.0.1:3004 and ignores WRTC_WS_PORT (src/bundle/Server.ts). Third, the client always uses wss://, so a plain ws voice server would also fail unless there is TLS or a client patch in assets/client_patches.

title: QR code on /login never appears: /remote-auth is answered by the normal gateway
steps: 1. Log out. 2. Open /login. 3. Wait on the right-hand 'Log in with QR Code' panel.
observed: The QR area shows a spinner forever. The client opens ws://fosscord.localhost:3145/remote-auth/?v=2 and receives the main gateway Hello {"op":10,"d":{"heartbeat_interval":30000}} instead of the remote-auth hello. The client logs 'received unsupported message', the socket closes with code 4002, and the client logs 'Could not complete Remote Auth login, trying to restart with a new Remote Auth session.' This loops for as long as the page is open.
expected: The remote-auth protocol should run (hello, init with encoded_public_key, nonce_proof, pending_remote_init with fingerprint) and render a QR code, or the QR panel should be hidden.
suspected_cause: src/bundle/TestClient.ts sets REMOTE_AUTH_ENDPOINT to ws(s)://host/remote-auth, but the server has no remote-auth handler. src/gateway/Server.ts accepts any path and speaks the normal gateway protocol.

title: Password reset cannot succeed: /auth/reset rejects the client's 'source' field
steps: 1. Open /reset#token=<any token>. 2. Enter a new password and click Change Password.
observed: POST /api/v9/auth/reset with body {"token":"...","password":"...","source":"/reset"} returns 400 {"code":50035,"errors":{"":{"_errors":[{"message":"must NOT have additional properties","code":"additionalProperties"}]}}}. The form shows no error and stays on 'Change Your Password'. Schema validation rejects the request before the token is checked, so a valid token fails the same way.
expected: The new password should be accepted, the user logged in, and invalid tokens shown as an error under the field.
evidence: 400 POST /api/v9/auth/reset
suspected_cause: src/schemas/uncategorised/PasswordResetSchema.ts only has password and token. It needs an optional source field, and the error shape needs to be one the form displays.

title: Reset-password email links to /reset-password, but the client route is /reset

observed: The client redirects /reset-password#token=... to /login, and the token is lost.
expected: The emailed link should open the 'Change Your Password' form. Discord uses /reset#token=...
suspected_cause: src/util/util/email/index.ts generateLink builds `${instanceUrl}/${dashedType}#token=`, which gives /reset-password for MailTypes.resetPassword. It also uses api.endpointPublic minus /api as the host.

title: 'Forgot your password?' shows no confirmation, and an empty email is silently accepted
steps: 1. On /login, type newbie3@fosscord.test into the email field. 2. Click 'Forgot your password?'. 3. Repeat with the email field empty.
observed: Both cases return 204 POST /api/v9/auth/forgot with an empty body (with {"login":""} and with a real email). No 'Instructions sent' modal opens and no error shows under an empty email field.
expected: With a valid email, Discord opens a modal saying instructions were sent to <email>. With an empty or unknown login, it returns 400 with errors.login and the field shows the error.
evidence: The client does `return d.h.dispatch({type:"FORGOT_PASSWORD_SENT"}),t.body.method`. With a 204 and no body this throws, the catch dispatches LOGIN_FAILURE, and the success modal never opens.
suspected_cause: src/api/routes/auth/forgot.ts always returns sendStatus(204). It should return a JSON body the client can read (e.g. {"method": ...}) and validate that login is present.

title: Logging out does not invalidate the token
steps: 1. POST /api/v9/auth/login as newbie3 to get token T. 2. POST /api/v9/auth/logout with authorization T, body {"provider":null,"voip_provider":null} (returns 204). 3. GET /api/v9/users/@me with authorization T.
observed: Step 3 returns 200 with the full user object. The session row is deleted, but the token keeps working. UI logout (Settings > Log Out > confirm) also only clears localStorage, so anyone holding the old token keeps access.
expected: After logout the token should get 401 everywhere, including gateway identify.
suspected_cause: src/util/util/Token.ts checkToken loads the Session by decoded.did but never rejects when it is missing (the `session ?? undefined` path), so tokens whose session was removed by src/api/routes/auth/logout.ts still validate.

screen: App load with invalid or expired token
title: An invalid token leaves the client on the loading screen forever instead of returning to /login
steps: 1. Set localStorage.token to "garbage.token.value" (or any token the server rejects). 2. Open /channels/@me.
observed: The 'Did you know' loading screen stays forever. The gateway closes with code 4000 'Failed to decode token', and the client reconnects in a loop. REST GET /api/v9/users/@me returns 400 {"code":40001,...} instead of 401.
expected: Discord closes the gateway with 4004 Authentication failed and REST returns 401. The client then logs out and shows /login.
evidence: Node WebSocket identify with a bad token prints: close 4000 Failed to decode token.
suspected_cause: src/gateway/opcodes/Identify.ts awaits checkToken(), which rejects (Token.ts line 148 `rejectAndLog(reject, 500, "Failed to decode token")`). The rejection becomes a generic 4000 close instead of CLOSECODES.Authentication_failed. The auth middleware in src/api/middlewares also answers 400 instead of 401 for code 40001.

title: The voice channel timer next to the channel name shows 'NaN:NaN'

title: An invalid or expired token leaves the client stuck on the loading splash instead of logging out
steps:
1. Put a bad token in localStorage, e.g. token = "MTU1NTU2ODY3NzA3NDU2MzE2OQ.garbage.token".
2. Open /channels/@me and wait 15 s.
observed: The client shows the 'DID YOU KNOW' loading splash forever, followed by 'Connection problems? Let us know! Tweet Us / Server Status'. The gateway closes the socket with 4000 'Unsupported token algorithm: undefined', so the client keeps reconnecting. REST GET /api/v9/users/@me with a bad or missing token returns HTTP 400 with code 40001 instead of 401.
expected: Discord closes the gateway with 4004 'Authentication failed' and REST returns 401 Unauthorized. The client then clears the token and redirects to /login.
evidence: A node WebSocket identify with the bad token got CLOSE 4000 "Unsupported token algorithm: undefined". curl /api/v9/users/@me returned 400 {"code":40001,...}.
suspected_cause: src/gateway/opcodes/Identify.ts awaits checkToken(), which rejects (src/util/util/Token.ts:156, rejectAndLog 400). The exception goes to the generic handler in src/gateway/events/Message.ts and closes with Unknown_error (4000) instead of reaching the CLOSECODES.Authentication_failed branch. DiscordApiErrors.UNAUTHORIZED in src/util/util/Constants.ts:741 uses the ApiError default httpStatus of 400 instead of 401.

After that, TOTP turns on, backup codes are shown, and security keys can be registered.
evidence: 400 POST /api/v9/users/@me/mfa/totp/enable must have required property 'password'; 400 POST /api/v9/users/@me/mfa/webauthn/credentials must match a schema in anyOf
suspected_cause: src/api/routes/users/@me/mfa/totp/enable.ts and totp/disable.ts (TotpEnableSchema/TotpDisableSchema require password/code) and the webauthn/credentials schema don't implement the MFA reauth (60003 ticket) flow the Oct 2026 client expects.

The gateway closes the IDENTIFY with code 4000 'Invalid Token' instead of 4004, so the client re-identifies in a loop and sits on the 'DID YOU KNOW' loading screen forever. A garbage token also gets close 4000 'Invalid Token meow TypeError: "ES512" signatures must be "132" bytes'.
expected: Discord returns HTTP 401 for an invalid token and closes the gateway with 4004 Authentication failed. The client then clears the token and shows the login page.

suspected_cause: src/util/util/Constants.ts UNAUTHORIZED ApiError has no 401 status, and src/api/middlewares/Route.ts throws it as a 400. In src/gateway/opcodes/Identify.ts, checkToken() rejects and the exception is caught in src/gateway/events/Message.ts, which closes with CLOSECODES.Unknown_error (4000) instead of Authentication_failed (4004).

screen: DM view, Wave to say hi
title: Wave in a DM is saved as a broken reply ('Message could not be loaded') and can reference a random message
steps: Log in as tester, open the seeded DM with friend (/channels/@me/<dm>), click the 'Wave to friend' button under the messages.

The server stores a type 19 (REPLY) message with message_reference {type:0} and no message_id, so the wave sticker renders under a reply header 'Message could not be loaded'. The route also resolves the target with Message.findOneOrFail({where:{id: undefined, channel_id: undefined, guild_id: undefined}}), which TypeORM treats as no filter and returns an arbitrary message from any channel, then sets it as referenced_message.

suspected_cause: src/api/routes/channels/#channel_id/greet.ts: always sets type REPLY and message_reference {...payload.message_reference, type:0}; findOneOrFail with undefined where-values when message_reference is absent.
